scope: Official current deployment parity for already-supported Compound III, Morpho Blue and SparkLend on chain1,10,56,137,143,8453,42161. Only exact official Comet market proxies, Morpho Blue core singletons and SparkLend pools; no new labels, grants, runtime languages, scopes or arbitrary vaults. Parent exclusively integrates additions and lifecycle removals.
admissionNotes: Static official deployment/source/ABI review only, not a current runtime-identity attestation, funding, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or complete-workflow guarantee. Exact-function grants, canonical ABI/value checks, pauses and independent execution controls remain mandatory; no grants or profiles change.

Each new target has its own independently fetched complete ABI/source response; same-address or same-bytecode assertions on another chain are never substituted. Sourcify match, creationMatch, runtimeMatch and reported implementation identity are preserved verbatim. Institutional Comet uses independently address-bound Blockscout partial verification and exact-extension Sourcify evidence, explicitly not exact-match implementation evidence.

Full source code is deduplicated by SHA256 into sourcePool. responseProjection explicitly omits redundant metadata/AST/compiler artifact/bytecode copies; it retains full ABI, compiler/deployment/proxy identities, constructor or immutable binding values and all source files. originalResponseSha256 hashes the fetched raw response, not this projection.

All ABI function entries in each new available proxy/implementation/extension are inventoried individually; constructor/fallback/receive/events/errors are not capabilities. Arbitrum USDC.e implementation surface is unavailable rather than guessed; only its actual proxy ABI is inventoried.
Callback-free Morpho policy scopes are retained verbatim on supply,repay,supplyCollateral,liquidate; code-level scope binding review permits the new exact roots without modifying the runtime scope.

No abiHash is copied from another capability: parent must compute each new hash from its own exact ABI fragment during normal catalog integration. Existing labels and capability IDs remain unchanged except mandatory lifecycle removals.

compoundIII.discoveryNote: Current official docs link Compound-Foundation/comet, whose maintained map includes institutional_usdc not present in the older compound-finance/comet discovery snapshot. The canonical current map is authoritative.
compoundIII.unsupportedChainExclusion: hardhat is nonproduction; Linea,Mantle,Ronin,Scroll,Unichain have no supported chain here. No BSC56 or Monad143 official Comet deployments appear in this finite canonical map.
compoundIII.existingCoverageCorrection: Actual catalog0x3afdc9... Ethereum is USDT, not USDS; actual0x6f7d514... Arbitrum is WETH, not USDC.e. Existing financial methods were already10 per root, not2. These are evidence corrections, not aliases or renames.

morphoBlue.section: Morpho Blue only, excluding Midnight, vaults, factories, IRMs and testnets

sparkLend.conclusion: All src network registries reviewed; no additional SparkLend POOL on chain10,56,137,143,8453,42161. Spark Liquidity Layer/Spark Vaults/PSMs are not SparkLend pools and are outside this label/version scope.

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// OpenZeppelin Contracts (last updated v5.1.0) (interfaces/IERC4626.sol)

pragma solidity ^0.8.15;

import { IERC20 } from "./IERC20.sol";
import { IERC20Metadata } from "./IERC20Metadata.sol";

/**
 * @dev Interface of the ERC-4626 "Tokenized Vault Standard", as defined in
 * https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4626[ERC-4626].
 */
interface IERC4626 is IERC20, IERC20Metadata {
    event Deposit(address indexed sender, address indexed owner, uint256 assets, uint256 shares);

    event Withdraw(
        address indexed sender,
        address indexed receiver,
        address indexed owner,
        uint256 assets,
        uint256 shares
    );

    /**
     * @dev Returns the address of the underlying token used for the Vault for accounting, depositing, and withdrawing.
     *
     * - MUST be an ERC-20 token contract.
     * - MUST NOT revert.
     */
    function asset() external view returns (address assetTokenAddress);

    /**
     * @dev Returns the total amount of the underlying asset that is “managed” by Vault.
     *
     * - SHOULD include any compounding that occurs from yield.
     * - MUST be inclusive of any fees that are charged against assets in the Vault.
     * - MUST NOT revert.
     */
    function totalAssets() external view returns (uint256 totalManagedAssets);

    /**
     * @dev Returns the amount of shares that the Vault would exchange for the amount of assets provided, in an ideal
     * scenario where all the conditions are met.
     *
     * - MUST NOT be inclusive of any fees that are charged against assets in the Vault.
     * - MUST NOT show any variations depending on the caller.
     * - MUST NOT reflect slippage or other on-chain conditions, when performing the actual exchange.
     * - MUST NOT revert.
     *
     * NOTE: This calculation MAY NOT reflect the “per-user” price-per-share, and instead should reflect the
     * “average-user’s” price-per-share, meaning what the average user should expect to see when exchanging to and
     * from.
     */
    function convertToShares(uint256 assets) external view returns (uint256 shares);

    /**
     * @dev Returns the amount of assets that the Vault would exchange for the amount of shares provided, in an ideal
     * scenario where all the conditions are met.
     *
     * - MUST NOT be inclusive of any fees that are charged against assets in the Vault.
     * - MUST NOT show any variations depending on the caller.
     * - MUST NOT reflect slippage or other on-chain conditions, when performing the actual exchange.
     * - MUST NOT revert.

pragma solidity 0.8.15;

contract WETH9 {
    string public name     = "Wrapped Ether";
    string public symbol   = "WETH";
    uint8  public decimals = 18;

    event  Approval(address indexed src, address indexed guy, uint wad);
    event  Transfer(address indexed src, address indexed dst, uint wad);
    event  Deposit(address indexed dst, uint wad);
    event  Withdrawal(address indexed src, uint wad);

    mapping (address => uint)                       public  balanceOf;
    mapping (address => mapping (address => uint))  public  allowance;

    receive() external payable {
        deposit();
    }
    function deposit() public payable {
        balanceOf[msg.sender] += msg.value;
        emit Deposit(msg.sender, msg.value);
    }
    function withdraw(uint wad) public {
        require(balanceOf[msg.sender] >= wad);
        balanceOf[msg.sender] -= wad;
        payable(msg.sender).transfer(wad);
        emit Withdrawal(msg.sender, wad);
    }

    function totalSupply() public view returns (uint) {
        return address(this).balance;
    }

    function approve(address guy, uint wad) public returns (bool) {
        allowance[msg.sender][guy] = wad;
        emit Approval(msg.sender, guy, wad);
        return true;
    }

    function transfer(address dst, uint wad) public returns (bool) {
        return transferFrom(msg.sender, dst, wad);
    }

    function transferFrom(address src, address dst, uint wad)
        public
        returns (bool)
    {
        require(balanceOf[src] >= wad);

        if (src != msg.sender && allowance[src][msg.sender] != type(uint).max) {
            require(allowance[src][msg.sender] >= wad);
            allowance[src][msg.sender] -= wad;
        }

        balanceOf[src] -= wad;
        balanceOf[dst] += wad;

        emit Transfer(src, dst, wad);

        return true;
    }
}

Compound III

Introduction

Compound III is an EVM compatible protocol that enables supplying of crypto assets as collateral in order to borrow the base asset. Accounts can also earn interest by supplying the base asset to the protocol.

The initial deployment of Compound III is on Ethereum and the base asset is USDC.

Please join the #development room in the Compound community Discord server as well as the forums at comp.xyz; Compound Labs and members of the community look forward to helping you build an application on top of Compound III. Your questions help us improve, so please don’t hesitate to ask if you can’t find what you are looking for here.

For documentation of the Compound v2 Protocol, see docs.compound.xyz/v2.

Networks

The network deployment artifacts with contract addresses are available in the Comet repository deployments/ folder.

The v3 proxy is the only address to be used to interact with a Compound III instance. It is the first address listed in each of the tabs below. To generate the proper Comet Interface ABI (CometInterface.sol), compile the Comet project using yarn compile.


Note: The deployment data shown below is sourced from the compound-docs-aggregator repository. Data collected on: 2026-09-16 15:56:48.594 UTC.

Protocol Contracts

cUSDCv3

This is the main proxy contract for interacting with the first Compound III market. The address is fixed and independent from future upgrades to the market. It is an OpenZeppelin TransparentUpgradeableProxy contract.

cUSDCv3 Implementation

This is the implementation of the market logic contract, as deployed by the Comet Factory via the Configurator.

Do not interact with this contract directly; instead use the cUSDCv3 proxy address with the Comet Interface ABI.

cUSDCv3 Ext

This is an extension of the market logic contract which supports some auxiliary/independent interfaces for the protocol. This is used to add additional functionality without requiring contract space in the main protocol contract.

Do not interact with this contract directly; instead use the cUSDCv3 proxy address with the Comet Interface ABI.

Configurator

This is a proxy contract for the configurator, which is used to set and update parameters of a Comet proxy contract. The configurator deploys implementations of the Comet logic contract according to its configuration. This pattern allows significant gas savings for users of the protocol by ‘constantizing’ the parameters of the protocol.

Configurator Implementation

This is the implementation of the Configurator contract, which can also be upgraded to support unforeseen changes to the protocol.

Proxy Admin

This is the admin of the Comet and Configurator proxy contracts. It is a ProxyAdmin as recommended/implemented by OpenZeppelin according to their upgradeability pattern.

Comet Factory

This is the factory contract capable of producing instances of the Comet implementation/logic contract, and invoked by the Configurator.

Rewards

This is a rewards contract which can hold rewards tokens (e.g. COMP, WETH) and allows claiming rewards by users, according to the core protocol tracking indices.

Bulker

This is an external contract that is not integral to Comet’s function. It allows accounts to bulk multiple operations into a single transaction. This is a useful contract for Compound III user interfaces. The following is an example of steps in a bulked transaction.

  • Wrap Ether to WETH
  • Supply WETH collateral
  • Supply WBTC collateral
  • Borrow USDC

In addition to supplying, borrowing, and wrapping, the bulker contract can also transfer collateral within the protocol and claim rewards.

Developer Resources

The following developer guides and code repositories serve as resources for community members building on Compound. They detail the protocol deployment process, construction of new features, and code examples for implementing external apps that depend on Compound III as infrastructure.

  1. Compound III Developer FAQ
  2. Scenarios, Migrations, and Workflows
  3. Creating a Compound III Liquidator
  4. Building a Comet Extension

Security

The security of the Compound protocol is our highest priority; our development team, alongside third-party auditors and consultants, has invested considerable effort to create a protocol that we believe is safe and dependable. All contract code and balances are publicly verifiable, and security researchers are eligible for a bug bounty for reporting undiscovered vulnerabilities.

We believe that size, visibility, and time are the true test for the security of a smart contract; please exercise caution, and make your own determination of security and suitability.

Audits

The Compound protocol has been reviewed & audited by OpenZeppelin and ChainSecurity.

  1. Compound III Audit by OpenZeppelin

Deprecation of Polygon and Unichain Comets

Simple Summary

Gauntlet recommends the following changes to risk parameters to deprecate all active comets on Polygon (USDC and USDT) and on Unichain (USDC and WETH). These markets have seen limited adoption in the last 180 days, with borrow volume either decreasing or remaining flat. The proposed changes set all collateral supply caps to 0, reduce borrow collateral factors by 50% for all assets other than MaticX, which is set to 0, and set the supply interest rate to zero across all four comets so that all borrower-paid interest accrues to reserves during the deprecation period. Liquidation factors are left unchanged throughout.

The proposed changes set both supply rate slopes (below and above the kink) to 0% as well, so that suppliers earn no interest during the deprecation period and the full amount of borrower-paid interest accrues to protocol reserves. Rationale

The Polygon USDC, Polygon USDT, Unichain USDC, and Unichain WETH comets have seen limited adoption relative to the protocol’s other larger markets in the last 90 days, with collateral balances and borrow activity that do not justify continued active market operation. Gauntlet recommends deprecating all four comets.

Supply Cap Reduction to Zero

Setting all collateral supply caps to 0 prevents new capital from entering these markets. Existing positions are unaffected. The change closes the market to new entrants without disrupting current users.

Collateral Factor Reduction by 50%

Reducing borrow collateral factors by 50% materially reduces capital efficiency for all assets other than MaticX, making these markets significantly less attractive for new or expanded borrowing activity. All proposed collateral factors have been set well below the current liquidation factors for each asset, ensuring no existing borrower is pushed into liquidation as a direct result of these changes.

Supply Rate Set to Zero

We propose setting the supply interest rate to zero on all four comets by zeroing both supply rate slopes. Because Compound v3 does not expose a reserve factor parameter, the split between interest paid by borrowers and interest earned by suppliers is determined entirely by the two separate rate curves. Setting the supply rate to zero is the mechanism through which all borrower-paid interest is directed to reserves, which is the v3 equivalent of a 100% reserve factor.

This preserves and grows reserves throughout the wind-down rather than allowing them to be drawn down. As borrow balances decline toward zero, reserve accrual naturally tapers.

We want to be direct about the effect on existing suppliers. During the deprecation period, suppliers in these comets will earn 0% on their balances. Combined with the supply caps being set to 0, this removes the incentive to hold or add supply in these markets and encourages remaining suppliers to withdraw and redeploy to active Compound markets. Existing suppliers remain able to withdraw at any time; no funds are locked by this change. Given the low adoption of these markets, we view the tradeoff as appropriate for an orderly deprecation.

Liquidation Factors Unchanged

Liquidation factors are left unchanged across all assets on all four comets. This preserves the existing liquidation buffer for current users and avoids triggering forced liquidations.

Next Steps

We welcome community feedback.

Thanks for sharing this plan on today’s community call and providing details here. I’m not opposed, but I would like to understand Gauntlet’s rationale for not including the Mantle USDe comet at this stage of deprecation. By supply and borrow volumes, the Mantle comet is larger than both of the Unichain comets but meaningfully smaller than the Polygon comets. It is also arguably among the more labor-intensive comets from a risk-management perspectives with both the base asset and most collaterals on the Mantle USDe comet being unique to that market.

There is also the question of the strategic value to the DAO of supporting or deprecating these comets, which is not addressed in this post. I’m confident that the Foundation will offer feedback directly if these deprecations are counter to its V4 strategy, but if Gauntlet has its own perspective on strategic value of these comets to the DAO, that would also be interesting to hear.

FWIW, I for one welcome deprecation of the awkward USDC.e comet on Polygon, which launched awkwardly before Polygon made Circle’s official USDC on Polygon the chain-preferred asset (we should also consider this action for Base’s USDC.e comet). Unichain is more of a take-it-or-leave-it case to me; I agree the comet is not heavily utilized, but I still think there is some value in having a market here for UniV4 hooks that may benefit from access to a lending market on Unichain, value that may resurface in the future.

Thanks for the thoughtful feedback and for raising these points.

On strategic value, our recommendation here is driven by market health and operational rationalization rather than a view on V4 strategy, and we agree the Foundation is best placed to speak to how these markets fit the forward roadmap. That said, our per-comet reasoning is below.

Unichain: the primary driver for the recommendation is the sustained decline in on-chain activity across the entire chain, not just the Compound markets. Unichain DeFi TVL has fallen from a peak above $800M in mid-2025 to roughly $26.3M today, a decline that has continued steadily for the better part of a year with no sign of reversal (source: DefiLlama). Against that backdrop the Compound markets are very small: the Unichain USDC comet currently carries about $86K in borrows and $122K in supply, and the Unichain WETH comet about $343K in borrows and $382K in supply. We take your point on the potential future value of a lending market for UniV4 hooks. Our view is that this is speculative at present, and if that demand materializes, the market can be redeployed with parameters suited to the activity at that time. Maintaining active markets today based on potential future demand entails ongoing risk-management overhead that current utilization does not justify.

Polygon USDC.e: We agree with your framing. This comet launched before Polygon designated Circle’s native USDC as the chain-preferred asset, and it is the right time to ramp it down. We would also support evaluating the same action for the Base USDbC comet as a follow-up.

Polygon USDT: borrow demand on this comet has been persistently thin. Over the trailing 180 days borrows averaged roughly $0.9M and peaked around $1.5M, and the market currently sits at about $486K borrowed. We do not see a credible growth path for this comet, and believe deprecation is the cleaner outcome.

Across all four comets, existing borrowers remain solvent under the proposed collateral factors with no positions pushed into the CF/LF limbo zone, and withdrawals stay open throughout. Happy to go deeper on any individual market.

Simple Summary

Gauntlet recommends the following changes to risk parameters to deprecate all active comets on Polygon (USDC and USDT) and on Unichain (USDC and WETH). These markets have seen limited adoption in the last 180 days, with borrow volume either decreasing or remaining flat. The proposed changes set all collateral supply caps to 0, reduce borrow collateral factors by 50% for all assets other than MaticX, which is set to 0, and set the supply interest rate to zero across all four comets so that all borrower-paid interest accrues to reserves during the deprecation period. Liquidation factors are left unchanged throughout.
